label: Early original-phase step just after a g (1-2 steps back)
explanation: Fires during the original-input phase at early positions (t=1..5, peaking at t=3-4) when the letter g was input one or two steps earlier. Any current input token works. It is strongest the step right after g: prev_tok=g alone gives precision 0.94 and holds about 59% of the mass, and the largest activations come in sequences that start with g g g. At t=1 right after a leading g the activation is weak. It does not fire in the copy phase, at t=0, or at t>=6, even if g came just before; it rarely fires at the delimiter. The missed activations are low-magnitude, scattered and have no g nearby (about 8% of the mass). Adding g three steps back raises recall a little but lowers precision.

issues: One claim is partly wrong. The explanation says the missed activations have 'no g nearby', but about 3.9% of the 8.5% missed mass comes from steps where g was input exactly 3 steps back. That class fires with precision 0.41, so it is a decaying tail of the same g signal, not noise. The other misses, with no g seen before the step, fire at only about 2% and carry 2.4% of the mass. Those are scattered and low-magnitude.
Count recall is only 0.68 on test. Bottom-quartile coverage is 0.28, so the predicate captures the strong activations well but not the weak ones. Mass recall is 0.915.

How strong the feature is depends on where the g sits, which the label does not say. The step after a g at position 1, 2 or 3 is very reliable (precision 0.99-1.0). The step after a g at position 4 (t=5) gives 0.70, and the step after a g at position 0 (t=1) gives 0.94 precision but only 1.7% of the mass. Two steps after a g at position 4 (t=6) gives just 0.09, which matches the claimed t<=5 cutoff.

The other claims check out. Copy phase: 0 activations. t=0: 0 activations. t>=6: 0.4% of mass. Delimiter: 1.8% of mass (precision 0.14 even with g just before). Peak at t=3-4: 38% and 28% of mass. prev_tok=g alone: precision 0.94 and 60.5% of mass. Adding g 3 back on test: precision 0.79, F1 0.784. Test scores reproduce (P 0.903, R 0.683, F1 0.778, mass recall 0.915). The current input token does not matter: rates are flat across tokens.
